title: Work, Energy, Power & Collisions
syllabus: Work done by a constant force and a variable force, Kinetic and potential energies, Work-energy theorem, Power, Potential energy of a spring, Conservation of mechanical energy, Conservative and non-conservative forces, Motion in a vertical circle, Elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration $a_c$ varies with time $t$ as $a_c = k^2 r t^2$, where $k$ is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the forces acting on it is: (NEET 2018)
questions.solution:
Centripetal acceleration $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = k^2 r t^2 \implies v = k r t$.
Tangential acceleration $a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = k r$.
Tangential force $F_t = m a_t = m k r$.
Since centripetal force does no work, total power delivered is by tangential force:
$$P = F_t v = (m k r)(k r t) = m k^2 r^2 t$$

questions.question: A body of mass $1\text{ kg}$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F} = (2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})\text{ N}$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are unit vectors along x and y axis. What power will be developed by the force at the time $t$? (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
Acceleration $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = (2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})\text{ m/s}^2$.
Velocity $\vec{v} = \int \vec{a}\,dt = \left(t^2\hat{i} + t^3\hat{j}\right)\text{ m/s}$.
Power $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (2t)(t^2) + (3t^2)(t^3) = (2t^3 + 3t^5)\text{ W}$.

questions.question: A moving block having mass $m$, collides with another stationary block having mass $4m$. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is $v$, then the value of coefficient of restitution $(e)$ will be: (NEET 2018)
questions.solution:
Conservation of linear momentum:
$$m v + 4m(0) = m(0) + 4m v_2 \implies v_2 = \frac{v}{4}$$
Coefficient of restitution:
$$e = \frac{\text{Velocity of separation}}{\text{Velocity of approach}} = \frac{v_2 - 0}{v - 0} = \frac{v/4}{v} = 0.25$$

questions.question: A bullet of mass $10\text{ g}$ leaves a rifle at an initial velocity of $1000\text{ m/s}$ and strikes the earth at the same level with a velocity of $500\text{ m/s}$. The work done in overcoming the resistance of air will be: (NEET 2022)

Two similar springs $P$ and $Q$ have spring constants $k_P$ and $k_Q$, such that $k_P > k_Q$. They are stretched, first by the same amount (case a,) and then by the same force (case b). The work done by the springs $W_P$ and $W_Q$ are related as, in case (a) and case (b), respectively: (NEET 2015)
questions.solution:
Case (a): Same elongation $x$. $W = \frac{1}{2}kx^2 \propto k$. Since $k_P > k_Q \implies W_P > W_Q$.
Case (b): Same force $F$. $W = \frac{F^2}{2k} \propto \frac{1}{k}$. Since $k_P > k_Q \implies W_Q > W_P$.

questions.question: A force $F = 20 + 10y$ acts on a particle in $y$-direction where $F$ is in newton and $y$ in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from $y = 0$ to $y = 1\text{ m}$ is: (NEET 2019)

An engine pumps water continuously through a hose. Water leaves the hose with a velocity $v$ and $m$ is the mass per unit length of the water jet. What is the rate at which kinetic energy is imparted to water? (NEET 2020)
questions.solution:
Mass flow rate $\frac{dM}{dt} = m \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = m v$.
Rate of kinetic energy imparted (Power):
$$P = \frac{dK}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{dM}{dt}\right) v^2 = \frac{1}{2} (m v) v^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v^3$$

questions.question: A body of mass $(4m)$ is lying in $x\text{-}y$ plane at rest. It suddenly explodes into three pieces. Two pieces, each of mass $(m)$ move along the perpendicular axes with equal speed $(v)$. The total kinetic energy generated due to explosion is: (NEET 2014)
questions.solution:
Remaining third piece has mass $M_3 = 4m - m - m = 2m$.
By linear momentum conservation: $\vec{p}_3 = -(mv\hat{i} + mv\hat{j}) \implies p_3 = \sqrt{(mv)^2 + (mv)^2} = \sqrt{2}mv$.
Velocity of 3rd piece $v_3 = \frac{\sqrt{2}mv}{2m} = \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}$.
$$K_{\text{total}} = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 + \frac{1}{2}m v^2 + \frac{1}{2}(2m)\left(\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{3}{2}mv^2$$

questions.question: A block of mass $M$ is attached to the lower end of a vertical spring. The spring is hung from a ceiling and has force constant value $k$. The mass is released from rest with the spring initially unstretched. The maximum extension produced in the length of the spring will be:
questions.solution:
By conservation of mechanical energy between initial unstretched state and lowest extreme point:
$$\Delta U_{\text{grav}} + \Delta U_{\text{spring}} = 0 \implies -Mg x_{\text{max}} + \frac{1}{2}k x_{\text{max}}^2 = 0$$
$$x_{\text{max}} = \frac{2Mg}{k}$$

questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = (5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\text{ N}$ is applied over a particle which displaces it from its origin to the point $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - \hat{j})\text{ m}$. The work done on the particle in joules is:

A uniform chain of length $L$ and mass $M$ is lying on a smooth horizontal table and one-third of its length is hanging vertically down over the edge of the table. If $g$ is acceleration due to gravity, the work required to pull the hanging part on to the table is:
questions.solution:
Hanging mass $m = \frac{M}{3}$. Its center of mass is at a depth $h_{\text{cm}} = \frac{L/3}{2} = \frac{L}{6}$ below the table.
Work required to pull the chain onto the table:
$$W = m g h_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{M}{3}\right) g \left(\frac{L}{6}\right) = \frac{MgL}{18}$$

questions.question: The potential energy of a particle in a force field is $U = \frac{A}{r^2} - \frac{B}{r}$, where $A$ and $B$ are positive constants and $r$ is the distance of particle from the center of the field. For stable equilibrium, the distance of the particle is:
questions.solution:
For equilibrium, $F = -\frac{dU}{dr} = 0$.
$$-\frac{dU}{dr} = -\left(-\frac{2A}{r^3} + \frac{B}{r^2}\right) = \frac{2A}{r^3} - \frac{B}{r^2} = 0 \implies \frac{2A}{r^3} = \frac{B}{r^2} \implies r = \frac{2A}{B}$$
Since $\left.\frac{d^2U}{dr^2}\right|_{r=2A/B} > 0$, this point represents stable equilibrium.

questions.question: A body of mass $m$ tied to a string of length $L$ is whirled in a vertical circle. The difference between the tension in the string at the lowest point and the highest point is:
questions.solution:
Tension at lowest point: $T_L = \frac{m v_L^2}{L} + mg$.
Tension at highest point: $T_H = \frac{m v_H^2}{L} - mg$.
From conservation of energy: $v_L^2 - v_H^2 = 4gL$.
$$T_L - T_H = \frac{m(v_L^2 - v_H^2)}{L} + 2mg = \frac{m(4gL)}{L} + 2mg = 4mg + 2mg = 6mg$$

questions.question: A mass $m$ moving horizontally with velocity $v$ collides elastically with another identical mass $m$ at rest. After collision, the velocity of the first mass becomes:
questions.solution:
In a 1D head-on elastic collision between two equal masses ($m_1 = m_2$), they completely exchange their velocities.
Therefore, $v_1' = u_2 = 0$ and $v_2' = u_1 = v$.

questions.question: If the kinetic energy of a body is increased by $300\%$, the percentage increase in its momentum will be:
questions.solution:
$p = \sqrt{2mK}$.
When kinetic energy increases by $300\%$, $K' = K + 3K = 4K$.
New momentum $p' = \sqrt{2m(4K)} = 2\sqrt{2mK} = 2p$.
Percentage increase in momentum $= \frac{2p - p}{p} \times 100\% = 100\%$.

questions.question: Which of the following forces is NON-CONSERVATIVE in nature?
questions.solution: Friction force is non-conservative because the work done by friction along a closed path is non-zero (work is dissipated as thermal energy).

questions.question: A particle moves from point $P(1, 2, 3)$ to point $Q(2, 4, 6)$ under a constant force $\vec{F} = (3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})\text{ N}$. The work done by the force is:
questions.solution:
Displacement vector $\Delta\vec{r} = \vec{r}_Q - \vec{r}_P = (2-1)\hat{i} + (4-2)\hat{j} + (6-3)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.
$$W = \vec{F} \cdot \Delta\vec{r} = (3)(1) + (2)(2) + (4)(3) = 3 + 4 + 12 = 19\text{ J}$$

questions.question: A ball is dropped from a height $h$ on a horizontal floor. If the coefficient of restitution is $e$, the total distance travelled by the ball before coming to rest is:
questions.solution:
$$H_{\text{total}} = h + 2h_1 + 2h_2 + \dots = h + 2(e^2 h) + 2(e^4 h) + \dots$$
$$H_{\text{total}} = h + 2e^2 h(1 + e^2 + e^4 + \dots) = h + \frac{2e^2 h}{1 - e^2} = h\left(1 + \frac{2e^2}{1 - e^2}\right) = h\left(\frac{1+e^2}{1-e^2}\right)$$

questions.question: An electric motor produces a tension of $4500\text{ N}$ in a load-lifting cable and rolls it at the constant rate of $2\text{ m/s}$. The power of the motor is:
questions.solution: Power $P = F \cdot v = 4500\text{ N} \times 2\text{ m/s} = 9000\text{ W} = 9\text{ kW}$.

questions.question: A ball of mass $m$ moving with speed $u$ undergoes an oblique perfectly elastic collision with a smooth stationary identical ball. The angle between their final velocities after collision is:
questions.solution: For two identical masses undergoing a non-head-on (oblique) elastic collision with one initially at rest, the angle between their final velocity vectors is always $90^\circ$.

questions.question: A body of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is thrown upward with an energy of $490\text{ J}$. The height at which its kinetic energy becomes half of its initial value is: $(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2)$
questions.solution:
By conservation of mechanical energy:
$$\Delta U = \Delta K = K_i - \frac{1}{2}K_i = \frac{1}{2}(490) = 245\text{ J}$$
$$mgh = 245 \implies (2)(9.8)h = 245 \implies 19.6h = 245 \implies h = 12.5\text{ m}$$

questions.question: A spring with spring constant $k$ is compressed by an amount $x$. A ball of mass $m$ held against it is released. The speed of the ball when the spring reaches its natural length is:
questions.solution:
Elastic potential energy is completely converted into kinetic energy:
$$\frac{1}{2}k x^2 = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 \implies v = x\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$$

questions.question: In a perfectly inelastic collision between two bodies:
options: Linear momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not conserved
Both linear momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
Neither linear momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
Kinetic energy is conserved but linear momentum is not conserved
questions.solution: In any isolated collision, linear momentum is strictly conserved. In perfectly inelastic collisions, colliding bodies stick together and kinetic energy loss is maximized.

questions.question: A body of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ travels in a straight line with velocity $v = k x^{3/2}$ where $k = 5\text{ m}^{-1/2}\text{s}^{-1}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 2\text{ m}$ is:

A bob attached to a light inextensible string of length $L$ is given a minimum horizontal speed $v_0$ at the lowest point such that the string becomes slack when the bob is at the level of the center of suspension (horizontal string position). The speed $v_0$ is:
questions.solution:
At the horizontal level, $h = L$. For string to just become slack, tension $T = 0$.
Horizontal radial force equation: $T = \frac{m v^2}{L} = 0 \implies v = 0$.
By conservation of energy: $\frac{1}{2}m v_0^2 = mgL + 0 \implies v_0 = \sqrt{2gL}$ (for string slacking at angle $\theta = 90^\circ$). If it oscillates up to horizontal, $v_0 = \sqrt{2gL}$. If string slackens at horizontal, $v_0 = \sqrt{3gL}$.

questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = -k(y\hat{i} + x\hat{j})$ (where $k$ is a positive constant) acts on a particle moving in the $x\text{-}y$ plane. The force is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = -k \int (y\,dx + x\,dy) = -k \int d(xy) = -k(x_f y_f - x_i y_i)$$
Since the work done depends only on the initial and final coordinates (path independent), the force is conservative.

questions.question: A ball of mass $m$ hits a floor with speed $v$ at an angle of incidence $\theta$ with the normal to the floor. If the coefficient of restitution is $e$, the angle of reflection $\phi$ with the normal is given by:
questions.solution:
Parallel velocity component is unchanged: $v_t' = v\sin\theta$.
Normal velocity component: $v_n' = e(v\cos\theta)$.
$$\tan\phi = \frac{v_t'}{v_n'} = \frac{v\sin\theta}{e v\cos\theta} = \frac{\tan\theta}{e}$$

questions.question: A particle is released from height $S$ above the ground. At a certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the ground and its speed at that instant are respectively:
questions.solution:
Total energy $E = mgS$.
At height $h$: $U = mgh$ and $K = 3U = 3mgh$.
$E = K + U = 4mgh = mgS \implies h = \frac{S}{4}$.
$$K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 3mg\left(\frac{S}{4}\right) \implies v^2 = \frac{3gS}{2} \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{3gS}{2}}$$

questions.question: A pump on the ground floor of a building can pump up water to fill a tank of volume $30\text{ m}^3$ in $15\text{ min}$. If the tank is $40\text{ m}$ above the ground, and the efficiency of the pump is $30\%$, how much electric power is consumed by the pump? $(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2, \rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3)$
questions.solution:
Mass of water $m = 30 \times 1000 = 30000\text{ kg}$.
Output power $P_{\text{out}} = \frac{mgh}{t} = \frac{30000 \times 10 \times 40}{15 \times 60} = \frac{12000000}{900} = 13333.3\text{ W}$.
$$P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta} = \frac{13333.3}{0.30} \approx 44444\text{ W} = 44.4\text{ kW}$$

questions.question: A particle of mass $m_1$ moving with velocity $u$ makes a head-on elastic collision with a stationary particle of mass $m_2$. The fraction of kinetic energy transferred to the second particle is:
questions.solution:
Final velocity of mass $m_2$: $v_2 = \frac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}u$.
Fractional kinetic energy transferred:
$$\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}m_2 v_2^2}{\frac{1}{2}m_1 u^2} = \frac{m_2 \left(\frac{2m_1 u}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2}{m_1 u^2} = \frac{4m_1 m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2}$$

questions.question: A vertical spring with force constant $k$ is fixed on a table. A ball of mass $m$ at a height $h$ above the free upper end of the spring falls vertically on the spring so that the spring is compressed by a distance $d$. The net work done in the whole process is:
questions.solution: By Work-Energy Theorem: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K = K_f - K_i = 0 - 0 = 0$.

questions.question: The relationship between conservative force $F$ and potential energy $U$ in one dimension is:
questions.solution: Conservative force is defined as the negative gradient of potential energy: $F = -\frac{dU}{dx}$.

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ is driven by a machine that delivers a constant power $k$ watts. If the particle starts from rest, the force on the particle at time $t$ is:
questions.solution:
$P = k \implies \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = k t \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{2kt}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{2k}{m}} t^{1/2}$.
Acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \sqrt{\frac{2k}{m}} \left(\frac{1}{2}t^{-1/2}\right) = \sqrt{\frac{k}{2m}} t^{-1/2}$.
Force $F = m a = m \sqrt{\frac{k}{2m}} t^{-1/2} = \sqrt{\frac{mk}{2}} t^{-1/2}$.

questions.question: A light spring is compressed by $x_1$ and its stored elastic potential energy is $U_1$. When it is further compressed by another $x_1$ (total compression $2x_1$), the total stored energy becomes:
questions.solution:
$U_1 = \frac{1}{2}k x_1^2$.
When total compression is $x_2 = 2x_1$:
$$U_2 = \frac{1}{2}k(2x_1)^2 = 4\left(\frac{1}{2}k x_1^2\right) = 4U_1$$

questions.question: A body of mass $m$ is suspended by a string of length $l$. What minimum horizontal velocity should be imparted to it at the lowest point so that it can just complete a full vertical circle?
questions.solution:
To loop the loop, the critical velocity at the highest point must be $v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gl}$.
By conservation of mechanical energy:
$$\frac{1}{2}m v_{\text{low}}^2 = \frac{1}{2}m(gl) + mg(2l) = \frac{5}{2}mgl \implies v_{\text{low}} = \sqrt{5gl}$$

questions.question: A force $F = -k x^2$ acts on a particle moving along the x-axis. The work done by this force in moving the particle from $x = 0$ to $x = d$ is:

A ball of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ collides head-on with an identical ball at rest. If the coefficient of restitution is $e$, the ratio of velocities of the two balls after collision $(v_1 / v_2)$ is:
questions.solution:
By conservation of momentum: $v_1 + v_2 = v$.
By Newton's restitution law: $v_2 - v_1 = e v$.
Solving both equations gives $v_1 = \frac{v(1-e)}{2}$ and $v_2 = \frac{v(1+e)}{2}$.
$$\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{1-e}{1+e}$$

questions.question: The work done in stretching a spring by an additional extension $x$ from an initial stretched state of $x$ is:
A body is moved along a closed loop path in a gravitational field. The total work done by the gravitational force is:
questions.solution: Gravity is a conservative force field. The line integral of any conservative force over a closed path is identically zero: $\oint \vec{F}_g \cdot d\vec{r} = 0$.

questions.question: Two bodies with masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ have equal kinetic energies. If $p_1$ and $p_2$ are their respective linear momentums, then the ratio $p_1 / p_2$ is:
questions.solution:
Momentum $p = \sqrt{2mK}$.
Since $K_1 = K_2$:
$$\frac{p_1}{p_2} = \frac{\sqrt{2m_1 K}}{\sqrt{2m_2 K}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_1}{m_2}}$$

questions.question: A body of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is sliding down an inclined plane of angle $30^\circ$ from a height of $5\text{ m}$. If the work done against friction is $20\text{ J}$, the kinetic energy of the body at the bottom of the plane is: $(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2)$
questions.solution:
Total initial potential energy $U = mgh = 2 \times 10 \times 5 = 100\text{ J}$.
By conservation of energy: $K_f = U - W_{\text{friction}} = 100 - 20 = 80\text{ J}$.

questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = (2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on a body of mass $2\text{ kg}$ initially at rest. The instantaneous power delivered by the force at $t = 3\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})\text{ m/s}^2$.
At $t = 3\text{ s}$, velocity $\vec{v} = \vec{a}t = 3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$.
Power $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (2)(3) + (4)(6) = 6 + 24 = 30\text{ W}$.

questions.question: A stone of mass $m$ tied to a string is rotated in a vertical circle of radius $R$. If the string just becomes slack at the top, the tension in the string when the stone is at the bottom of the circle is:
questions.solution:
For string slacking at the top: $v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gR} \implies v_{\text{low}} = \sqrt{5gR}$.
At the bottom point:
$$T = \frac{m v_{\text{low}}^2}{R} + mg = \frac{m(5gR)}{R} + mg = 5mg + mg = 6mg$$

questions.question: A body of mass $m_1$ moving with speed $u$ collides head-on elastically with a stationary body of mass $m_2$. What is the condition for maximum transfer of kinetic energy from the first body to the second body?
questions.solution: Fractional energy transferred is $\frac{4m_1 m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2}$. This expression reaches its maximum value of $1$ ($100\%$ energy transfer) when $m_1 = m_2$.

questions.question: A force $F$ acting on a particle varies with displacement $x$ as shown by a trapezoid on an $F\text{-}x$ graph, where $F$ increases linearly from $0$ to $10\text{ N}$ between $x = 0$ and $x = 2\text{ m}$, remains constant at $10\text{ N}$ from $x = 2\text{ m}$ to $x = 4\text{ m}$, and decreases to $0$ at $x = 6\text{ m}$. The total work done is:
questions.solution:
Work done is the area of the trapezoid under the $F\text{-}x$ graph:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times (\text{sum of parallel sides}) \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times [(6 - 0) + (4 - 2)] \times 10 = \frac{1}{2} \times (6 + 2) \times 10 = 40\text{ J}$$
